sources.title: PPWR - Packaging minimisation
sources.supports: PPWR Article 10(1) requires packaging weight and volume to be reduced to the minimum necessary for functionality, taking account of the packaging's shape and material.

sources.title: PPWR - Minimum recycled content
sources.supports: PPWR Article 7 establishes minimum recycled-content requirements for plastic packaging according to the relevant packaging type and format; the threshold must be selected from the legal category rather than assumed to be uniform for all cosmetic bottles.
sources.citation: Article 7(1) and Article 7(8); Annex II, Table 1
sources.effective_date: 1 January 2030 or 3 years after entry into force of the implementing act referred to in Article 7(8), whichever is later

sources.title: PPWR - Packaging material labelling
sources.supports: Article 12(1) provides for a harmonised label identifying packaging material composition to facilitate consumer sorting, subject to the statutory start date and implementing acts.
sources.effective_date: 12 August 2028 or 24 months after entry into force of implementing acts under Article 12(6) or (7), whichever is later

sources.title: PPWR - Design for recycling
sources.supports: Article 6 establishes the recyclability framework, including design-for-recycling criteria and recycling-at-scale milestones; the criteria and grades are phased in rather than applying as one undifferentiated deadline.
sources.effective_date: Generally from 1 January 2030 or 24 months after the relevant delegated acts enter into force, whichever is later; further recycling-at-scale milestone in 2035; grades A or B required from 1 January 2038, subject to the regulation's details and exceptions

sources.title: Directive (EU) 2024/825 - Generic environmental claims and offsetting claims
sources.supports: The Directive targets generic environmental claims that cannot be substantiated by relevant recognised excellent environmental performance, and separately prohibits product greenhouse-gas neutrality, reduction, or positivity claims based on offsetting.
sources.citation: Article 1(4), amending Annex I to Directive 2005/29/EC, points 2a and 4a-4c; Recital 9 for examples of generic claims
sources.effective_date: Applies from 27 September 2026; check national implementation for the intended market

sources.title: Cosmetics Regulation - Safety and packaging labelling
sources.supports: Article 19 requires specified product and consumer information on cosmetic-product containers and packaging, while Article 3 establishes the general cosmetics safety requirement under normal or reasonably foreseeable conditions of use.
sources.effective_date: General application date 11 July 2013, subject to subsequent amendments and current applicable text

sources.title: Outer-carton removal - Transit damage validation
sources.supports: ISTA Procedure 3A is a general simulation performance test for packaged products shipped individually through parcel-delivery systems; it does not establish a universal rule that a shampoo bottle is safe to ship without an outer carton.
sources.citation: ISTA Test Procedures page, General Simulation Tests, Procedure 3A: Parcel Delivery System Shipments 150 lb (70 kg) or Less

sources.title: Full-body shrink sleeve - Bottle sorting and recyclability
sources.supports: Sleeves can interfere with bottle identification and recyclate quality, but the effect depends on sleeve material, colour, coverage, perforation, and the specific recycling stream; the sources do not establish that every sleeve is unrecyclable.
sources.citation: RECOUP, Recyclability of Bottles with Sleeves, Version 8, p. 2 and relevant discussion of detection, sleeve materials, and solutions. Secondary source: https://recyclass.eu/protocols-guidelines/design-for-recycling-guidelines/packaging/ (RecyClass current Packaging Design for Recycling Guidelines)

sources.title: Mono-material pump - Plastic spring/ball alternative
sources.supports: RecyClass reports that a specific fully plastic, polyolefin-based pump with a plastic spring and ball was tested as compatible with the HDPE recycling stream under a stated condition that the pump not exceed 26% of total packaging weight; this does not establish that every metal-spring pump makes a bottle unrecyclable.
sources.citation: RecyClass, Apackaging Group receives a RecyClass Recyclability Approval for Infinity Pump; stated HDPE-container evaluation protocol and pump weight condition. Secondary source: https://aptar.com/en-us/products/future-fully-recyclable-dispensing-pump (Aptar Beauty, Future - Fully Recyclable Dispensing Pump)

sources.title: PCR PET - Commercial availability for cosmetic bottles
sources.supports: Supplier catalogues list PET cosmetics/personal-care bottles with PCR options; ALPLA lists a 500 mL cosmetics bottle configurable up to 100% rPET with an MOQ of 35,000 units, demonstrating an actual commercial offering but not universal availability, price, colour, odour, or formulation compatibility.
sources.citation: ALPLA Standard Products, 500 ml Cosmetics Bottle 27 g, product specification including PCR options and MOQ. Secondary source: https://packagingsolutions.amcor.com/en/product/product-item/250ml-european-pet-13823010 (Amcor Packaging Solutions, 250ml European PET)

sources.title: Refill pouches - Flexible packaging recycling route
sources.supports: CEFLEX guidance prefers mono-PE or mono-PP flexible structures over mixed-material structures for improved sortability and recycling performance, but this does not prove a universal EU collection and recycling route for every refill pouch.
sources.citation: CEFLEX D4ACE Guidelines, Design Principles and Design Choices. Secondary source: https://www.ellenmacarthurfoundation.org/tackling-flexible-plastic-packaging-waste (Ellen MacArthur Foundation, Tackling Flexible Plastic Packaging Waste)

sources.title: Aluminium bottle - Internal lacquer and product compatibility
sources.supports: Supplier guidance describes internal linings for aluminium toiletry bottles and identifies formulation pH, fragrance/oils, alcohol, surfactant system, filling process, closure, and shelf life as compatibility considerations; it does not establish that every shampoo needs the same lacquer or that a coating is universally compatible with recycling.
sources.citation: PPG, PPG launches non-BPA PPG HOBA coatings for aluminum bottles at Paris Packaging Week (3 February 2025). Secondary source: https://blueskysolutionsuk.com/insight-resource/aluminium-packaging-for-toiletries/ (BlueSky Solutions, Aluminium Packaging for Toiletries, sections on internal lacquer/lining and compatibility)

sources.title: Glass versus plastic - Transport emissions for 250 mL shampoo
sources.supports: No reliable source was verified that quantifies the transport-only emissions difference between otherwise comparable 250 mL glass and plastic shampoo bottles under a defined EU distribution scenario.

sources.title: Rigid PLA - EU sorting/recycling and end-of-life route
sources.supports: CBE JU reports industrial sorting trials involving PLA cups/trays and other bio-based plastic items, while the European Commission describes the wider end-of-life policy context; these sources indicate infrastructure and sorting considerations but do not prove that rigid PLA bottles are compostable-only or universally accepted in EU kerbside streams.
sources.citation: CBE JU, Sorting out the future of bio-based plastics recycling, published 21 August 2026, sections Testing under real-world conditions, Results at industrial scale, and What's next. Secondary source: https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/plastics/bio-based-biodegradable-and-compostable-plastics_en (European Commission, EU policy framework on biobased, biodegradable and compostable plastics)

sources.title: Rigid PET, HDPE and PP - Recyclability baseline
sources.supports: RecyClass maintains stream-specific design-for-recycling guidance for PET bottles and HDPE/PP containers; an individual package's recyclability depends on its full design, components, applicable stream, and relevant PPWR criteria rather than polymer identity alone.
sources.citation: RecyClass current Packaging Design for Recycling Guidelines. Secondary source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32025R0040 (PPWR Article 6(1)-(5) and Article 6(8), Recyclable packaging)
